sampling_model.design: A deterministic partition into exactly \(B\) positive batches. Before outcomes are generated, each count rule is a Borel map \(q_b:(\mathsf H_{b-1},\mathcal G_{b-1})\to(\mathbb Z,2^{\mathbb Z})\). Evaluating it at the canonical prefix gives the \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\)-measurable count \(Q_b=q_b(O^{(b-1)})\), after which the batch is completely randomized conditional on \(Q_b\).
sampling_model.units: The canonical observed record lies in \(\mathsf H_B=(\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\) with its product Borel sigma-algebra. The law is built recursively by appending a randomized assignment vector and then independent Gaussian responses from the assigned-arm kernels; no joint coupling of unobserved arm outcomes is posited.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with every realized batch share constrained to \([1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.overlap: Pathwise exact-count overlap: \(\lceil m_b/4\rceil\le q_b(h)\le\lfloor3m_b/4\rfloor\) for every canonical prefix \(h\in\mathsf H_{b-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Arm variances are learned from deterministic prefixes of each observed arm stream and projected onto \([\ell^2,u^2]\); no random-size chi-square assertion is used.

body.tldr: Policy updates are treated as a scarce experimental-design resource. The core result is a uniform every-\(B\) minimax frontier for the normalized excess MSE of observed-data Gaussian adaptive Neyman experiments with exact counts: the chronological variance-learning term is \(B\{(n+1)^{1/B}-1\}/n\), while compulsory exact batching adds a lattice term of order \((B/n)^2\). The at-most-\(B\) envelope saturates at order \((\log n)/n\), whereas forcing nearly \(n/4\) batches can be strictly harmful. A deterministic-prefix plug-in design matches the frontier up to constants and supports a uniformly valid fixed-time Wald interval. The sharp chronological constant and the literal factor-two saturation threshold remain a first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing adaptive Neyman papers supply first-order efficiency, fixed-stage upper rates, unrestricted lower bounds, or low-switching constructions, but no matched actual-MSE frontier indexed by every exact update count with integer allocations and deterministic batch-contrast weights.
project_justification.niche: Exact batching introduces two losses that average-propensity and reward-regret analyses suppress: observations cannot repair the allocation within their own batch, and each positive batch has its own treatment-count lattice.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact risk identity, proves matching constructive upper and chronological-information lower rate bounds, distinguishes exactly from at most \(B\), anchors the endpoints, and attaches studentized fixed-time inference to the attaining design. The observed experiment is specified directly through chronological assignment and response kernels, so every frontier and coverage claim is invariant to any unobserved within-unit potential-outcome coupling.

body.related_work: Li and Simchi-Levi characterize sequential efficiency through average propensity and give low-update constructions; their timing-collapsed benchmark informs the oracle but does not define the every-update frontier. Zhao derives fixed-stage competitive upper exponents and an unrestricted adaptive proxy-risk lower bound; the present target uses actual weighted-estimator MSE and a fixed-\(B\) converse. Hirano and Porter's endogenous-information-set representation motivates the chronological local experiment. Armstrong's adaptive efficiency bound supplies a least-favorable-score template at first order. Perchet, Rigollet, Chassang, and Snowberg and Gao, Han, Ren, and Zhou develop recursive grids and feedback-gap lower bounds for reward regret, which inform the constructive upper bound under a different loss. Cai and Rafi expose fixed-pilot failures, while Yamin gives conditional minimax-regret pilot rules and a boundary-driven global pilot rate; their results motivate the separate compact-interior two-wave anchor. Wright isolates static integer-allocation loss. Blackwell, Pashley, and Valentino motivate volume-weighted exact-count batch contrasts. Noarov, Fogliato, Bertran, and Roth obtain per-unit Neyman regret scaling up to log factors under bounded finite-population conditions; the public Amazon adaptive-abtester repository implements that sequential design family and supplies the operational consumer. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, Chen and Andrews, Niu and Ren, and Dai, Gradu, and Harshaw supply distinct inference templates for fixed-batch, two-stage, conditional, or per-unit adaptive experiments. No theorem-level tightening of these differently defined comparators is asserted; they are method and problem-formulation ancestors. The model here is instead defined directly as an observed adaptive-experiment law: assignment histories and the single revealed response per unit are jointly generated by explicit chronological kernels, without an unidentified counterfactual copula.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-scale path in \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{LAN}}\) holds \(s\) fixed. If common scale is allowed to vary as an unknown nuisance along the local path, the efficient information for the variance-ratio parameter depends on the treated and control counts, so the information-two calculation cannot be imported unchanged. The sharp-constant analysis must preserve this distinction.
body.honest_scope: The two-sided order frontier, exact one-batch formula, two-batch exponent, envelope order, overscheduling witness, and uniform Wald theorem are formal targets. The exact leading constant of \(\Psi_\infty(n)\), a uniformly matching sharp schedule, the exact finite-sample two-batch minimax rule, and the factor-two saturation threshold remain open. Under the standard one-batch special case, the frontier reduces to balanced assignment against the worst orientation of the variance box; under two batches it reduces to the square-root-pilot exponent already suggested by multistage upper constructions but adds a matching actual-MSE converse. Every formal risk, minimax, variance-estimation, and coverage object is a functional of the explicit observed-data law; no joint distribution of unobserved arm outcomes is required.
